items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret?
premises: The teaching is to be concealed.
Concealment requires deliberate effort.
The mortal world contains the lowest of men.
items.inference: The teaching must be carefully hidden in the mortal world among unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching legitimately be given?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient must be previously accomplished.
The recipient must be tested for one year.
items.inference: The teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa.
The section is numbered as fifth.
The section is called a chapter.
items.inference: The fifth chapter of the text emerged from Candradvīpa concludes here.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace has the determination of Kaula been understood?
premises: The speaker claims knowledge.
The knowledge concerns the determination of Kaula.
The knowledge arose by the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.inference: The determination of Kaula has been understood through the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have understood the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in the teaching.
Its identity is asked about.
Its essential nature is asked about.
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve according to this teaching?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution.
The locus of dissolution is questioned.
The speaker requests a complete explanation.
items.inference: The teaching must explain the locus into which the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality being described?
premises: The subject is identified as supreme.
The subject is partless and eternal.
The subject is free from disease and stain.
items.inference: The ultimate reality is supreme, partless, eternal, and free from all defect.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa and śakti?
premises: The soul is described as supreme.
That supreme soul is identified as haṃsa.
That supreme soul is identified as the individual of power.
items.inference: The supreme soul is the haṃsa, the individual constituted by power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul which is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath.
This air is described as situated.
Its location is in all living beings.
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam may reflect transmitted text.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called upon merely leaving the body?
premises: The subject is considered at the moment of leaving the body.
At that moment it is given a designation.
The designation is supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is the secret teaching transmitted and perceived by the practitioner?
premises: Something is heard abiding in the ear.
The goddess is addressed as recipient.
It has come down through traditional succession.
items.inference: The teaching is heard in the ear as something transmitted through tradition.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the effect of merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The knowledge is described as mere knowledge.
It is received by hearing.
The fair-faced one is addressed.
items.inference: Even merely hearing this knowledge has significance for the addressed practitioner.
uncertainties: The main clause continues in the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard,

items.question: What disciplined practice leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months.
The practitioner undertakes a renunciant state.
That state is free from bondage.
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a renunciant state free from bondage.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to ochre robes or the ascetic condition.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months in that ochre, bondage-free state,

items.question: What result follows from sustained practice in the prescribed state?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases.
The practitioner associates with yogis.
Union with yogis is attained.
items.inference: Sustained practice results in freedom from disease and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī.
The subject communicated is the practice of the soul.
The communication is declared complete.
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has been told to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: What kind of recipient is worthy to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient must be endowed with all states.
The recipient must have a resolved mind.
items.inference: The teaching should be given to a fully endowed person of firm resolve.
uncertainties: Case mismatch between genitive and locative qualifiers may reflect transmitted text.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a firmly resolved mind.

items.question: To whom must the essential Kaula teaching not be given?
premises: The Kaula essence is highly valued.
Its origin is associated with the yoginīs.
The text explicitly prohibits giving it.
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: The intended excluded recipients are implied rather than named.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after receiving knowledge?
premises: The speaker refers to her own body.
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance.
Now the body is described as pure.
items.inference: Receiving knowledge has transformed the body from ignorance-struck to pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What further auspicious knowledge does the speaker now seek?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish.
The wish is to hear a teaching.
The teaching concerns the auspicious overcoming of time.
items.inference: The speaker now seeks instruction on the auspicious overcoming of time.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ can mean deception or overcoming depending on context.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death?
premises: The speaker promises to explain.
There is said to be no doubt.
The explanation concerns how death is destroyed.
items.inference: The teaching will explain without doubt how death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you without doubt how death is destroyed.

items.question: What condition affects even the wise at the tip of nectar?
premises: The locus is the tip of nectar.
An essence of juice is involved.
Even the wise one is described as burning.
items.inference: Even a wise person experiences a burning condition at the tip of nectar.
uncertainties: The physiological referent of amṛta+agraṃ is esoteric.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one is burning at the tip of nectar with the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic technique is prescribed at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: The practice is located at the root of tongue and palate.
The practitioner acts upon the breath.
The breath should be drawn in slowly.
items.inference: The practitioner should slowly drink the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing oneself at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink the breath.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year.
The practice becomes established.
Old age and death are subject to destruction.
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this technique destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity is claimed for the body of the accomplished practitioner?
premises: The body may be bitten by great serpents.
Poison would normally enter the body.
The text denies that poison enters.
items.inference: The accomplished practitioner's body becomes immune even to the poison of great serpents.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
